data.title: init installs the Claude Code hooks by default; --no-hooks opts out
data.why: The prompt hook is what makes agents use the journal (1 in 10 without it, 9 in 10 with it, KAD-53), and an opt-in flag is one more thing nobody passes: a feature that has to be switched on is a feature most repositories never get. The owner chose on 2026-09-29 to have init write .claude/settings.json itself, creating it where there is none, and say so. What kept the old rule honest stays: it is an upsert that keeps every other hook, it never rewrites a file that does not parse, the message names what was added and how to go without it, and the prompt hook never blocks a prompt. Measured cost on ordinary work: ten read-only code tasks, ~180 tokens more per prompt, no agent sent into the journal, same answers, same time.
data.rejected: Keep --hooks opt-in with a louder hint: the hint was already there and the hook was installed nowhere, including this repository; Install only when .claude/ already exists: a repository that has not used Claude Code yet is exactly where the first session starts without it
